title: Activity-Based Proteomics with 2D-PAGE for Identifying Target Proteases in Arabidopsis

steps.title: Prepare B5 vitamin stock (100×)
steps.instruction: Dissolve nicotinic acid (25 mg), pyridoxine hydrochloride (25 mg), thiamin hydrochloride (5 mg), myo‑inositol (5 g), and glycine (100 mg) in Milli‑Q water and bring the volume to 500 mL to obtain a 100× B5 vitamin solution.

steps.title: Prepare B5 growth medium
steps.instruction: Combine one bag (3.3 g) of Gamborg's B5 medium salt mixture with 10 mL of the 100× B5 vitamin solution, add sucrose to 1 % (w/v, 10 g), and bring to 1 L with Milli‑Q water; adjust pH to 5.7 with 1 N KOH, autoclave at 121 °C for 20 min, and for solid medium add 7 g agar before autoclaving.

steps.title: Make Rehydration solution A
steps.instruction: Dissolve CHAPS to 4 % (w/v, 40 mg) and add IPG buffer to 0.5 % (v/v, 5 µL) and DTT (0.62 mg/mL, 39 µL of 15.9 mg/mL stock) in Milli‑Q water and bring the volume to 1 mL.

steps.title: Make Rehydration solution B
steps.instruction: Dissolve CHAPS to 2 % (w/v, 20 mg), add IPG buffer to 0.5 % (v/v, 5 µL), bromophenol blue to 0.002 % (w/v, 40 µL of 0.05 % stock), and bring the volume to 1 mL with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Combine Rehydration solutions
steps.instruction: Mix 20 µL of solution A with 140 µL of solution B to obtain 160 µL of final rehydration solution.

steps.title: Prepare equilibration solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 6‑aminocaproic acid (0.59 g) to 450 mM, add glycerol (2.55 mL, 25.5 % v/v), Tris‑HCl (1 mL of 0.5 M, pH 6.8), CBB G‑250 (2 mg, 0.02 % w/v), and bring the volume to 10 mL with Milli‑Q water.

steps.title: Prepare native PAGE buffers
steps.instruction: For the anode buffer, dilute 20× Native PAGE running buffer 1× by mixing 10 mL of the 20× stock with 190 mL water (total 200 mL). For the cathode buffer, dilute 20× running buffer 1× by mixing 5 mL of the 20× stock, CBB G‑250 (0.4 % w/v, 500 µL), and water to 100 mL.

steps.title: Prepare in‑gel peptide assay solution
steps.instruction: Combine Nma‑flg[47–56]‑Dnp (1.7 mL of 40 µM), MES‑KOH (850 µL of 25 mM, pH 5.7), and Milli‑Q water to a final volume of 17 mL (14.45 mL water).

steps.title: Prepare fixing solution
steps.instruction: Mix methanol (20 mL, 20 % v/v) with acetic acid (7.5 mL, 7.5 % v/v) and Milli‑Q water (72.5 mL) to a total of 100 mL.

steps.title: Cultivate Arabidopsis submerged culture
steps.instruction: Transplant 40 six‑day‑old Arabidopsis thaliana Col‑0 seedlings (grown on B5 solid medium) into 100 mL B5 liquid medium in a 300 mL flask; incubate 7–11 days at 22 °C under continuous light without shaking (hand‑shake a few times daily).

steps.title: Concentrate and clarify culture medium
steps.instruction: Collect the spent medium by decantation, concentrate 100 mL to 10 mL using a rotary evaporator (water bath 37 °C), transfer to 15 mL centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 11,900 × g for 5 min (himac CF15RN, T11A31 rotor).

steps.title: Dialyze and lyophilize sample
steps.instruction: Dialyze the supernatant overnight at 4 °C with stirring against 3 L reverse‑osmosis water using a Spectra/Por 7 membrane (10 kDa cutoff); then centrifuge again at 11,900 × g for 5 min, transfer supernatant to a new tube, freeze at –80 °C and lyophilize.

steps.title: Resuspend lyophilized sample in rehydration solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve the lyophilized powder in 125 µL of the prepared rehydration solution and transfer to a 1.5 mL microtube.

steps.title: Centrifuge sample before IEF
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 125 µL sample solution at 18,800 × g for 5 min using a himac CF15RN (T15AP31 rotor).

steps.title: Load IPG strip and rehydrate
steps.instruction: Load the supernatant into a 7 cm IPG strip holder, place the immobilized pH‑gradient strip gel‑side down in the holder with the dehydration solution, add DryStrip cover fluid, and cover with the plastic lid.

steps.title: Run isoelectric focusing
steps.instruction: Place the holder on an Ettan IPGphor platform; rehydrate for 14 h at 20 °C, then run IEF at 50 µA/strip, 20 °C with the following steps: 500 V for 30 min, 1,000 V for 30 min, 5,000 V for 100 min (maximum voltage may not be reached; total rehydration must exceed 10 h).

steps.title: Equilibrate IPG strip for native PAGE
steps.instruction: Place the IEF‑finished IPG strip in 10 mL equilibration solution in a 15 mL tube and incubate at 4 °C for 15 min, then rinse briefly with native PAGE anode buffer.

steps.title: Set up native PAGE gel with IPG strip
steps.instruction: Remove wells from a 4–16 % Bis‑Tris native PAGE gel using a surgical blade and tweezers to create one protein‑marker well and one wide well; place the IPG strip into the wide well, gently press onto the gel surface (trim ends if needed) and avoid air bubbles.

steps.title: Run native PAGE electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Insert the gel into the electrophoresis apparatus, fill the upper tank with native PAGE cathode buffer and the lower tank with anode buffer, load 3 µL NativeMark unstained protein standard into the marker well, and run at 150 V for ~90 min (or until the dye front reaches the gel end).

steps.title: Excise gel and prepare for fractionation
steps.instruction: Using a surgical blade, cut off the top and bottom of the gel (removing the IPG‑strip contact surface and the region below the dye front) and also remove the marker lane; rinse the remaining gel piece with 25 mM MES‑KOH (pH 5.7) in a square Petri dish.

steps.title: Rinse gel and place on SAINOME plate
steps.instruction: Lay the rinsed gel onto a SAINOME 384‑well microplate.

steps.title: Cut gel into 384 wells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Position the SAINOME cutter on the gel, secure the cutter and plate together with tape, and centrifuge the assembly at 2,000 × g for 5 min using a himac CF16RN (T5S32 rotor) to cut the gel into 4.5 mm squares that fall into the 384 wells.

steps.title: Add peptide cleavage assay solution to wells
steps.instruction: Remove the cutter, then add 60 µL of the in‑gel peptide cleavage assay solution to each well containing gel pieces.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence over 16 h
steps.instruction: Using a plate reader, record fluorescence (excitation 340 nm, emission 435 nm) every hour for 16 h.

steps.title: Collect assay solution and gel fragments
steps.instruction: Separate assay solution from gel fragments; place assay solutions from fluorescence‑positive and fluorescence‑negative wells into separate 1.5 mL tubes, and likewise place the corresponding gel fragments into separate 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Fix gel fragments
steps.instruction: Incubate the gel fragments with fixing solution at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Reduce, alkylate, and digest proteins
steps.instruction: Transfer fixed gel fragments to a 96‑well filter plate with tweezers, perform reduction and alkylation using the Extrahera system as described in reference [21], then move the fragments to a new 1.5 mL tube and digest with Lys‑C and trypsin according to the same reference.

steps.title: Analyze digests by nano‑LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Inject 7.25 µL of each digest into a nano‑LC‑MS/MS system comprising a Q Exactive Hybrid Quadrupole‑Orbitrap mass spectrometer coupled to a Dionex U3000 gradient pump, following the procedure of reference [21].

steps.title: Process MS data and identify proteases
steps.instruction: Process raw files with Proteome Discoverer 2.3 using SEQUEST HT, searching against the TAIR10 Arabidopsis database; set peptide mass range 350–5,000 Da, enzyme trypsin (full) with up to 2 missed cleavages, minimum peptide length 6, max 3 equal modifications per peptide, precursor tolerance ±10 ppm, fragment tolerance ±0.02 Da, static carbamidomethyl (Cys) and dynamic oxidation (Met). Extract proteins with signal peptides using TAIR GO and SignalP 6.0, and identify secreted proteases enriched in the active fraction based on PSM and abundance scores.
